sections.h2: What To Expect On The Call

items.text: A conversation about your business, your goals for the site, and what is not working with what you have now, if anything.
Straight answers on platform choice, rough scope, and what a realistic budget range looks like for your project.
No pressure to decide on the call, and a short recap sent by email afterward so you are not relying on memory for what was discussed.
Booking a web design consultation does not commit you to hiring Teknoppy.

sections.h2: Why Businesses Trust Teknoppy's Consultation Calls

items.text: Every web design consultation is run by the same people who will design and develop your project, not a sales layer that hands you off afterward.
The call is a working conversation, not a scripted pitch ending in a hard close.
If Teknoppy is not the right fit for what you need, we will say so.

items.html: Nothing said on the call contradicts what is published on our pricing page.

paragraphs.text: A Kochi based clinic recently booked a web design consultation unsure whether they needed a full site or just a booking page.

The thirty minute web design consultation covered patient booking flow, whether WordPress or a custom build made sense, and a realistic budget range, ending with a clear recommendation and a same week follow up quote, not a pushed decision on the call itself.

devNotes.source: Leadgen pillar page-book a consultation inner page.pdf (Google Drive, teknoppybusiness@gmail.com)
devNotes.keyword: web design consultation — 11 occurrences, density band 1.8–2.0% per the source doc.
devNotes.notRendered: The doc's header block (word count, density, schema list) and its closing cannibalization check are build instructions, not page copy.
devNotes.heldCopy: NEEDS CLIENT — no booking calendar exists. Two sentences from the doc's 'Book Your Web Design Consultation' paragraph are held back because they describe a live calendar the site does not have: 'Booking a web design consultation with Teknoppy takes one step, pick a slot from the calendar that works for you.' and 'No form to fill out first, no waiting for a callback.' Rendering them above a form would contradict the form. In their place the section asks for a preferred date, time slot and call type, and the request is confirmed manually. Once a Calendly / Cal.com embed is chosen and added, restore both sentences and drop the date and time fields.
devNotes.formNote: Preferred date, time slot and call type are folded into the enquiry email by InnerPage's lead-form script, since api/contact.js has no column for them.
devNotes.operationalClaims: The page promises a 30-minute call over phone or video, run by the people who would do the work, plus a short email recap afterward. Confirmed with the client as deliverable before launch.
